election_types.name: Lok Sabha (General) Election
election_types.description: Election to the lower house of Parliament. Held every 5 years. Elects 543 Members of Parliament (MPs).

election_types.name: Vidhan Sabha (State Assembly) Election
election_types.description: Election to state legislative assemblies. Held every 5 years per state. Different states vote at different times.

election_types.name: Rajya Sabha Election
election_types.description: Upper house of Parliament. Members are indirectly elected by state legislative assemblies, not the general public.

election_types.name: Local Body Elections
election_types.description: Panchayat and Municipal elections conducted by State Election Commissions.

election_types.name: By-Elections
election_types.description: Held when a seat becomes vacant due to death, resignation, or disqualification of a sitting member.

disqualifications: Convicted and sentenced to 2+ years imprisonment

voter_registration.authority: Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of your constituency
steps: Visit voters.eci.gov.in or download Voter Helpline App
Upload proof of residence (Aadhaar/Utility Bill/Ration Card)
Submit and note your reference number
Wait for verification by Booth Level Officer (BLO)
Your name appears in the electoral roll within 30 days
documents_required: Proof of Age: Aadhaar Card / Birth Certificate / School Certificate / Passport
Proof of Residence: Aadhaar / Utility Bill / Bank Passbook / Ration Card

voter_id.download: Digital Voter ID (e-EPIC) available at voters.eci.gov.in

election_process_phases.name: Announcement of Election Schedule
election_process_phases.description: The Election Commission announces the election schedule, including polling dates, and the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) comes into force immediately.
key_events: Transfer of senior officials by government is restricted

election_process_phases.name: Nomination Filing
election_process_phases.description: Candidates file their nomination papers with the Returning Officer (RO) of the constituency.
key_events: Deposits security amount (₹25,000 for General; ₹12,500 for SC/ST)
Files affidavit disclosing assets, liabilities, criminal records
10 proposers from the constituency required (for non-party candidates)

election_process_phases.name: Scrutiny of Nominations
election_process_phases.description: The Returning Officer scrutinizes all nomination papers for validity.
key_events: RO checks age, citizenship, constituency membership
Objections can be raised by other candidates
election_process_phases.typical_duration: 1 day (the day after last date of nomination)

election_process_phases.name: Withdrawal of Candidatures
election_process_phases.description: Candidates can withdraw from the election up to 2 PM on the last date of withdrawal.
key_events: Candidate submits withdrawal notice to RO

election_process_phases.name: Election Campaign
election_process_phases.description: Political parties and candidates campaign to win voter support.
key_events: Campaign ends 48 hours before polling (Silent Period)

election_process_phases.name: Polling Day
election_process_phases.description: Voters cast their votes at designated polling booths using Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs).
key_events: Voter shows EPIC or alternate ID (Aadhaar, Passport, etc.)
Indelible ink applied to left index finger
Vote cast on EVM; VVPAT slip shown for 7 seconds
election_process_phases.typical_duration: 1 day (may be multiple phases across country)

election_process_phases.name: Counting of Votes
election_process_phases.description: EVM votes are counted at Counting Centres under strict supervision.
key_events: EVM counting begins round by round

election_process_phases.name: Declaration of Results & Formation of Government
election_process_phases.description: After all results are declared, the winning party/coalition forms the government.
key_events: Winning party invited to form government
President/Governor invites leader of majority to take oath

model_code_of_conduct.name: Model Code of Conduct (MCC)
model_code_of_conduct.description: A set of guidelines issued by the ECI to regulate political parties and candidates during elections.
key_rules: No party in power shall use government resources for campaigning
No announcement of new government schemes after MCC kicks in
No religious or communal appeals for votes
No distribution of cash, gifts, or liquor
Permission required for rallies and processions
No use of government vehicles for campaign purposes
model_code_of_conduct.enforcement: ECI can take action including cancelling candidature, FIR registration

evm.description: A tamper-proof machine used to cast and store votes electronically. Consists of a Control Unit (with polling officer) and Ballot Unit (with voter).

vvpat.description: Attached to EVM. After voting, displays a slip with the candidate name and symbol for 7 seconds, then drops into a sealed box.

key_officials.responsibility: Head of the Election Commission of India. Oversees entire election process.
Assists CEC. Currently there are 2 Election Commissioners alongside the CEC.
In charge of conducting election in a specific constituency.
Maintains the electoral roll for a constituency.
Manages voter registration at the booth level. First point of contact for voters.
IAS/IPS officer deputed by ECI to monitor election conduct in a constituency.

alternate_ids_for_voting: Bank / Post Office Passbook with photo

important_helplines.cvigil_app: cVIGIL App — report MCC violations with geotagged photo/video

faq.q: Can I vote if I don't have a Voter ID card?
faq.a: Yes! ECI allows 12 alternate photo identity documents including Aadhaar, Driving Licence, PAN Card, Passport, etc. Your name must be on the electoral roll.

faq.q: How do I find my polling booth?
faq.a: Visit voters.eci.gov.in or call 1950. You can also use the Voter Helpline App. Search by name or EPIC number to get your booth details.

faq.q: What if my name is not on the voter list?
faq.a: You cannot vote until your name is added. Register via Form 6 on voters.eci.gov.in. For immediate elections, approach the ERO or BLO with your documents.

faq.q: Can NRIs vote in Indian elections?
faq.a: Yes. NRIs can register as overseas electors using Form 6A. However, they must be physically present in their constituency to vote — there is no postal/proxy voting for NRIs yet.

NOTA stands for 'None of the Above'. It is an option on the EVM that allows voters to reject all candidates. Introduced in 2013. NOTA votes are counted but do not affect the result — the candidate with most votes still wins.

faq.q: How many phases does a Lok Sabha election have?
faq.a: It varies. The 2024 Lok Sabha election had 7 phases spread over April–June. Phases are decided by ECI based on security and logistical requirements.

faq.q: What is the Model Code of Conduct?
faq.a: The MCC is a set of ECI guidelines that restricts political parties and the government from using official machinery for campaign purposes. It kicks in the moment the election schedule is announced.

faq.q: How can I report election violations?
faq.a: Use the cVIGIL app to report Model Code of Conduct violations with a geotagged photo or video. ECI teams respond within 100 minutes.
